388 human brains · Science 2024 · try it

Why the brain is read cell type by cell type

Emani et al. profiled single nuclei from the prefrontal cortex of 388 adults (brainSCOPE, PsychENCODE) and built, for 28 cell types, maps of regulatory elements, expression QTLs, gene networks, and a model linking genotype to disorders through cell types. Two of its ideas on simulated data; boxes marked Paper quote the paper.

An eQTL that acts in one cell type is diluted in bulk tissue

ybulk = Σk sk yk  ⇒  effect in bulk ≈ sa × effect in cell type a

An expression QTL is a variant whose alleles shift a gene’s expression. Measured in one cell type, the shift is plain. Bulk tissue mixes all cell types, each in proportion sk, so a shift confined to cell type a shrinks by its share. Pick where the variant acts and how many people you have; each dot is one simulated person.

Paper About 85,000 single-cell eQTLs and 690 eGenes per cell type, about 1.4 million over all cell types; about 47% appear in more than one cell type. About 30% overlap known bulk-tissue eQTLs: their direction agrees, but the effect is larger in the cell type than in bulk, which the authors explain as a dilution effect. More than two-thirds are not found in bulk, despite the much larger bulk sample sizes (Fig. 4).

Toy: genotypes 0/1/2 with allele frequency 0.3; each cell type’s expression has person-to-person spread 1 plus measurement noise that grows as the cell type gets rarer (fewer nuclei); effect in units of that spread per allele. Shares are illustrative, not the paper’s. P values from least squares; the curve below shows the expected evidence.

Follow a variant through cell-type genes to a disorder’s risk

genotype → expression of gene g in cell type c (QTLs, regulatory networks) → risk;  saliency = ∂ risk / ∂ xg,c

The study’s integrative model has visible layers for genotypes, cell-type expression and networks, and a linear path to each disorder. Because it is linear, every gene in every cell type gets a readable importance, the gradient of the risk, and any node can be perturbed. Below is a six-node toy in that spirit: change a person’s genotype, or tap a node to knock that gene down in that cell type.

Importance of each gene in each cell type

Paper LNCTP imputes cell-type expression from genotype with a mean correlation of 0.69 to observed expression across major cell types and about 0.78 in excitatory and inhibitory neurons, explaining 38% of the variance against 34% for a baseline without the networks. It prioritizes 64, 51, 108 and 34 gene–cell-type pairs for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, autism and Alzheimer’s disease; RORA, for example, matters in many cell types for schizophrenia but is not prioritized from bulk data (Fig. 8).

Toy, hand-set: the real model is a conditional energy-based model plus a deep linear model, trained on the 388 individuals. Node values are in units of their population spread; a knockdown subtracts 1.5. The bulk comparison simulates 388 people from the same toy.

Toys, not results: simulated data that illustrate two ideas of the study. Study: Emani et al., Science 384, eadi5199 (2024).
